overall_summary: Space-themed content, particularly first-person 'What If' hypothetical survival scenarios on extreme exoplanets (e.g., diamond, burning ice, and coal-dark planets), significantly outperforms psychology, brain trivia, and basic animal facts. Immersive, high-contrast visual hooks and physical paradoxes drive the highest engagement and view counts.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-person 'What If' hypothetical survival scenarios on extreme exoplanets.
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,025 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (970 views, 18 likes) are top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize the 'What If You Fell Into...' framing for space content, focusing on sensory-rich, high-stakes survival details.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme planetary paradoxes in titles and hooks.
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views) and 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,055 views) achieved peak organic reach.
winning_patterns.action: Lead with mind-bending contradictions (e.g., hot ice, ruby rain, dark stars) to create immediate cognitive dissonance in the first 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently flopped.
weak_patterns.action: Halt production on standard cognitive psychology facts, or reframe them entirely under high-stakes survival or sci-fi contexts.

weak_patterns.pattern: Overused animal facts and basic biology trivia.
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (max 363 views across multiple re-uploads) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) underperformed compared to space topics.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic animal trivia; pivot to cinematic animal survival stories with deep narrative arcs if exploring biology.

next_video.opening_direction: If you stepped onto this beautiful blue planet, you wouldn't drown in water... you'd be shredded by glass raining sideways at 7,000 kilometers per hour.

next_video.reason: Combines the highly successful 'What If' survival format with the proven appeal of extreme planetary weather (similar to the supersonic rubies concept), optimized at the 21-second sweet spot.

experiment: Launch a 'Cinematic Animal Survival' micro-story focusing on the wood frog's winter freeze-and-thaw cycle, moving away from dry trivia into high-stakes, story-first wildlife drama.
